solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bean mole chewed: soil nutrient results

indicators.note: something chewed is mashed up and reshaped, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mole in the garden gnaws through a bean, and the soil is the richer for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' rearranges the eight letters of BEAN MOLE; 'results' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground animal bones are a classic phosphate-rich fertiliser that gardeners dig into beds.

clue.text: One installing part of store, we hear, who hopes to make money?

indicators.note: tells the solver the phrase is spoken, so its sound gives the entry

parts.note: a shop counter is part of a store, and the person who installs one is a counter fitter

explanation.surface: A shopfitter at work, wondering whether the job will pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals that COUNTER FITTER, said out loud, gives the answer. The definition is cryptic: this person 'makes' money literally, by forging it.
explanation.definitionFit: A forger of banknotes manufactures cash, a witty literal reading of making money.

clue.text: Check into Native American nursery

indicators.note: one piece going into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: An inspection of a nursery school run for Native American children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like a verb, but it gives the chess abbreviation, with 'into' as the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A day nursery for small children is a synonym, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Attractive piece in magazine on World Wide Web

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: the net is an everyday name for the internet and the web

explanation.surface: An attractive article in a magazine that is also published online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places MAG above NET in this down entry; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally attractive: a lump of iron or ferrite that pulls metal toward it.

clue.text: Horse-riding display misplaced in Times Square

indicators.note: letters put in the wrong places are rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse show staged, rather oddly, in the middle of New York's Times Square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' rearranges all thirteen letters of IN TIMES SQUARE.
explanation.definitionFit: The art and sport of riding horses, as shown off in dressage and show jumping events.

clue.text: Inscriptions on gravestone causing tears

definitions.meaning: R.I.P., rest in peace, is carved on gravestones; several of them
tears (rhyming with bears) are rents in cloth

explanation.surface: Epitaphs on a headstone that move mourners to weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' is read as rents, not weeping; 'causing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the abbreviation for rest in peace, and also splits or rents in fabric.

clue.text: Maybe The Queen is on in sixty minutes

indicators.note: on is placed in the hour, inside it

parts.note: sixty minutes make an hour

explanation.surface: A TV announcement that Her Majesty will appear within the hour.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the ace, king, queen, jack and ten of trumps are called honours, so 'Maybe The Queen' is a definition by example; 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the top trump cards, the queen among them, are called by this name.

clue.text: First two of accused left, free of all charges

indicators.note: asks for only the opening pair of letters of the next word

parts.note: to quit a place is to have left it

explanation.surface: The two main defendants walk out of court cleared of every charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is the past of leave, not the opposite of right.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that clears a defendant declares them not guilty of every count.

clue.text: Control shower when speaking

indicators.note: the word is to be said out loud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a shower of rain

explanation.surface: Someone trying to keep a shower under control while talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap used to guide a horse, and so, as a verb, to restrain or keep in check.

clue.text: Chat about old and new poetry

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A conversation about poems ancient and modern.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to talk informally with someone, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Southern Himalayan peak, most forbidding

parts.note: Everest is the highest Himalayan mountain

explanation.surface: The south face of a great Himalayan mountain is the most daunting climb.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of harsh or stern, matching the superlative forbidding.

clue.text: Took school exam

definitions.meaning: past tense of sit, as in to sit (take) an exam
the standard American college admissions test taken at school

explanation.surface: A pupil reports having taken a school test.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAT is the American admissions test, the Scholastic Aptitude Test.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of sit, as in sat a paper, and an American school-leavers' test.

clue.text: Drink first-class champagne ultimately

parts.note: top means first-class, the best

indicators.note: in the end, so the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An instruction to enjoy the finest champagne in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' is a verb here: to tope is to drink heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned verb for drinking alcohol habitually, from which comes toper, a drunkard.

clue.text: Here you'll see journalists hurry before fight

indicators.note: the first piece comes ahead of the second

parts.note: to press on is to hurry
to box is to fight

explanation.surface: Reporters rush to ringside before a boxing match.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved area at a sports ground set aside for reporters covering the event.

clue.text: Key article, first to be cut

indicators.note: the answer cuts into these words, sitting inside them across the comma

explanation.surface: An editor deciding which important piece goes first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cut' signals the answer sitting in 'artiCLE First'. 'Article' tempts you to look for A or THE, but it only hosts letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical symbol fixing the pitch of the stave; in French and heraldry it also means a key.

clue.text: Heavily taxed transport in South-East, beginning in Dover

indicators.note: the transport is placed in the South-East

parts.note: a train is a form of transport

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: Rail services in south-east England are stretched, starting with Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals containment and 'beginning in' takes an opening letter. Dover is a Channel port in south-east England; 'taxed' means burdened, not charged tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretched or taxed heavily means put under great stress, a past participle in both.

clue.text: Posh girl comes in to speak wisely

indicators.note: the girl enters the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: to say is to speak
GEL is the upper-class British pronunciation of girl

explanation.surface: An upper-class girl walks in and talks good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes in' signals containment. Writing girl as 'gel' imitates an old-fashioned upper-class English accent.
explanation.definitionFit: In the manner of a sage, a wise person, so with good judgement.

clue.text: After port, Edward went wild

indicators.note: the name comes after the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward, having drunk port, ran amok.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as the drink; here it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Running amok as a mob means taking part in a violent public disturbance.

clue.text: Starting to like tango when dancing with Kit

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places

explanation.surface: Someone discovering a love of the tango while partnering Kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when dancing' rearranges TANGO with KIT; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for beginning to feel fondness for someone or something.

clue.text: Tree, one found near river

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A lone tree growing beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The botanical genus of the maple, used for maple trees generally.

clue.text: Small number say nothing, finding food

parts.note: NO is the short form of number
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A few people keep quiet once they get their food.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for grub or a meal.

clue.text: Before entering California, you'll get some breakfast

indicators.note: the first word goes into the state abbreviation

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A promise of breakfast before you arrive in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' reads as a time word in the surface but is the archaic synonym; 'entering' signals containment and 'you'll get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornflakes and porridge are typical morning grain foods, so the definition gives an example.

clue.text: European Union's hundred miles an hour trains finish here

parts.note: EU is the European Union, with the S of the possessive
doing a ton is British slang for a hundred miles an hour

explanation.surface: European high-speed trains running at a hundred miles an hour terminate here.
explanation.walkthrough: EUSTON is a London railway terminus, where lines from the north-west end.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainline terminal station in London is where rail journeys end.
